**Position Overview**
---------------------

* 12-Month Internship | Commencing February 2027 | Full Time | $58,893 +15.4% super

* Lucas Heights, Sutherland Shire Location / Bus from Sutherland Station
* Health & Wellbeing Programs | Generous leave provisions | Cafe onsite

**About the Opportunity**
-------------------------

**A competitive edge over other Graduates!** Are you completing a degree in Science or Engineering and would like to gain valuable hands-on practical experience in your field? ANSTO's Year in Industry Internship program is your introduction to a career in nuclear science and technology at the home of Australia's most significant landmark and national infrastructure organisation.

**Be industry-ready!** The one-year program commences February 2027 and provides industry- based learning for students to apply theory and skills to the workplace and use this experience to enhance the value of their remaining study. You will get the opportunity to work with world- class, specialised scientific equipment to deliver on a range of industry and research projects. This opportunity is ideal for students studying one or more of the following degrees: .

* Chemistry
* Earth and environmental science
* Physics
* Forensic science
* Engineering
  

The internship is open to penultimate year students, and participants are required to defer their final year of study to work full-time. If selected for this opportunity you will need to provide a formal statement from your university confirming approval of your deferral of studies to participate in the program.

**About You**
-------------

*"This opportunity is ideal for someone with a strong technical foundation, proactive mindset, excellent collaborative skills and has a passion for science"* - **Isabella Naletilic, Radioanalytical Science Services Manager**

**Your Duties and Responsibilities**
------------------------------------

* experimental design and implementation
* maintenance, calibration and operation of laboratory equipment
* alpha, beta and gamma spectral analysis, including the maintenance, calibration, and operation of associated counting instrumentation
* radiochemical separations
* inorganic chemistry
* lead-210 dating of sediment
* laboratory housekeeping
* record keeping and data collation
* and more...

**About Us**
------------

ANSTO leverages great science to deliver big outcomes. We partner with scientists and engineers and apply new technologies to provide real-world benefits. Our work improves human health, saves lives, builds our industries and protects the environment. ANSTO is the home of Australia's most significant landmark and national infrastructure for research. Thousands of scientists from industry and academia benefit from gaining access to state-of-the-art instruments every year.

ANSTO's Nuclear Stewardship division maintains national nuclear science & technology capabilities and functions that are mandated by Government, regulators or otherwise considered essential to ongoing ANSTO operations. Capabilities include radionuclide metrology, measurement and monitoring of radioactivity in the environment, low and intermediate radioanalytical chemistry and nuclear forensics.

This position will be based in the Low Level Radioanalytical Group which maintains measurement capabilities to quantify naturally occurring radionuclides and difficult to measure radionuclides through alpha, beta and gamma measurement techniques, as well as lead-210 dating of sediments.

**Working with us you will enjoy**
----------------------------------

ANSTO employees are passionate about what they do. We enjoy being part of an organisation making a difference in the lives of Australians.

  

**Diversity and inclusion**
===========================

At ANSTO, we recognise that diverse teams deliver better outcomes. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can contribute and thrive.

We strongly encourage applications from:

* Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
* Women in STEM
* People with disability

**How to Apply**
----------------

All applications must be submitted through the online application system. Applications submitted via email will not be accepted.

For further technical information relating to this position please refer to the Position Description or contact Isabella Naletilic on (02) 9717 9187. For all other queries please contact Talent Acquisition on +61 **(02) 9717 9361.**

  

**Additional Information**

* The program is scheduled to commence in February 2027
* Opportunities are full-time paid placements
* Participants must defer their university studies for the duration of the program and provide confirmation from their university
* Appointment is subject to obtaining the required security and pre-employment medical assessment
* All applicants must be Australian citizens

**About Us**
------------

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like — and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds — which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia — many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact — this is the place.

**About the role**

Our Forward Deployed team works between our customers and our product. They take a customer’s whole support operation (the tickets, the systems, the policies) and turn it into AI agents that resolve real customer queries in production.

As an FDE intern, you’ll be part of that team from day one, not on a side project. The workflows you build will go live and handle real conversations for some of the largest fintech and healthtech companies in the US and Australia. You’ll have close support from the team and real ownership of the work you take on.

Day to day, you’ll:

* Dig into customers’ support tickets and data to find where AI can fully resolve queries, and where it can’t yet
* Build, test, and refine AI workflows from first draft through to production
* Help connect workflows to customer systems through APIs, and test integrations before they go live
* Join customer calls, share what you’ve found, and own defined parts of an implementation
* Use Claude Code and other AI tools to speed up analysis, build internal tooling, and improve how the team works

You’ll leave knowing how AI agents are deployed end to end at scale in regulated industries. You’ll also have hands-on skills in workflow design, API integrations, testing and evaluation, and LLM fundamentals, and experience turning a customer’s messy real-world problem into a working solution.

**We’d love to talk if you**

* Are curious and learn fast. You pick up new tools quickly and enjoy figuring things out.
* Are technically confident. You don’t need to be a software engineer, but you’re comfortable reading API docs and working with data.
* Sweat the details. You notice when something’s off, ask good questions, and follow through.
* Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical people alike.
* Are genuinely interested in AI. It’s a bonus if you’ve experimented with LLMs or built something with AI tools on your own.

**What's unique about this opportunity?**
-----------------------------------------

**A culture that's genuinely different.** Low ego, high trust, no tolerance for talented jerks. We work efficiently, keep hours flexible, and actually mean it — because life outside work matters. We're committed to building a diverse team and actively encourage applicants from underrepresented backgrounds. We care far more about user obsession and eagerness to learn than traditional credentials.

**A front-row seat to building something meaningful.** We're Series A and moving fast. You'll have real scope to shape the product and the company — not just execute someone else's vision.

**Performance recognized in real time, not on a calendar.** Promotions happen when you're ready — leadership meets every six weeks specifically to identify and recognize strong performers, so you're never waiting for an arbitrary review window to move up.

**We're AI-native, and we'll make you AI-native too.** Every person at Lorikeet uses AI in their day-to-day work (current favourite: Claude Code), with unrestricted access and no usage limits. You'll leave with skills that matter for the next decade of work.

**Twice a year, the whole company flies to Hawaii.** Headquartered in Sydney, with teams spanning the US and UK — which means getting everyone in the same place is something we invest in seriously. We spend the time hacking on ideas, building things together that wouldn't otherwise exist, and making memories that remind you why you joined a startup in the first place.

**A recruitment process built on respect, not hoops.** We keep it simple: a couple of informal chats to share our story and hear yours, followed by a paid ~two-day work trial. The work trial is genuinely the best part — you'll work on real problems alongside the actual team, get a true feel for how we operate, and we'll both come out of it knowing whether this is the right fit. No trick questions, no take-homes that disappear into a void. Just real work, done together.

If you're from an underrepresented background and don't tick every box, please reach out anyway. We know firsthand that diverse teams perform better, and we're proud that our team reflects a broad spectrum of identities and lived experiences.

* opportunity to learn and enhance your skills and experience in the unique teaching and research environment of a Veterinary Teaching hospital

Exciting opportunity for a Teaching and Leadership academic to contribute to innovative and impactful teaching and leadership in Psychology at Macquarie University, with particular contributions to Clinical Neuropsychology and Applied Psychology training.

The School of Psychological Sciences, within the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences (FMHHS) is seeking a suitably qualified academic to be actively involved in the development, curriculum design, teaching and delivery of units as well as supervision in the accredited Master of Clinical Neuropsychology postgraduate psychology course, the Master of Professional Psychology and the Undergraduate Psychology Courses within the School.

Joining our School at an exciting time of curriculum growth and renewal, you will play a meaningful part in developing new units and enriching the student experience across one of the largest and most highly regarded psychology courses in the country.

If you are passionate about teaching and supervising in applied psychology and neuropsychology, helping students build the skills that shape professional practice, we would be glad to hear from you.

The successful applicant will be expected to be available on a full-time basis by January 2027.

**About the Role**

As a Lecturer (Level B) or Senior Lecturer (Level C) you will be involved in unit development and/or re-design, delivery of teaching across our accredited Psychology courses, as well as supervising students in the Master of Clinical Neuropsychology and the Master of Professional Psychology. Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Contributing to unit development and teaching within accredited undergraduate and postgraduate Psychology courses including the Master of Neuropsychology.
* Delivering and managing teaching content, lectures, tutorials and assessments across face-to-face and/or online modalities.
* Teaching in applied psychology areas, including clinical neuropsychology, psychological assessment, neuropsychological rehabilitation, counselling and/or therapeutic skills, and developmental psychology.
* Helping to create an engaging and inclusive learning experience for undergraduate and postgraduate cohorts.

**About Us**

The School of Psychological Sciences is ranked among the top 75 Psychology Departments in the world and is at the forefront of research, teaching and community engagement. We offer accredited undergraduate and postgraduate programs in Psychology, with the largest suite of postgraduate programs in New South Wales.

The school sits within the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences (FMHHS), whose education suite includes clinical science, physiotherapy, medicine, exercise and sports science, public health, psychology, cognitive sciences, linguistics, audiology and speech pathology. The faculty forms part of MQ Health, an integrated academic health sciences enterprise incorporating Macquarie University Hospital and primary and speciality clinics.

We foster a values-based culture of innovation and creativity to achieve excellence in teaching and to enhance the research performance of the University. We invest in developing the careers and wellbeing of our students and staff, and we live our values of Caring, Integrity, Teamwork, Ambition, Innovation and Engagement.

**About You**

You will have a tertiary and professional qualifications in neuropsychology, and the capacity to design, deliver units and programs at both the undergraduate and the postgraduate levels. You will also have experience with, or a willingness to embrace, educational technology, blended learning and educational innovation.

**Essential Criteria for Level B (Lecturer) and Level C (Senior Lecturer)**

  

* A PhD or equivalent tertiary qualifications in Psychology.
* Current registration as a Psychologist (Practicing status) with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA).
* Current endorsement as a Clinical Neuropsychologist with AHPRA (and with minimum 18 months with full endorsement status).
* Demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality learning and teaching, including the design, delivery, and management of online and face-to-face content, lectures, tutorials, and assessments, with evidence of excellent student outcomes and reflective practice.
* Demonstrated experience in and/or with the teaching of major methods of evidence-based psychological and neuropsychological assessment, such as the Wechsler tests, personality inventories, and measures of general psychological distress and functioning across the lifespan.
* Demonstrated experience in teaching evidence-based therapeutic approaches and counselling skills across the lifespan.
* Demonstrated excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with an ability to relate to build an inclusive teaching and learning environment, and work effectively in a team environment.
* Evidence of successful delivery to diverse student cohorts and creating a superior student experience characterised by strong engagement at the postgraduate and undergraduate levels.
* Evidence of quality coursework research supervision (e.g., Honours).

**Essential for Level C (Senior Lecturer)**

  

* Demonstrated leadership experience in the delivery of units and programs, working collaboratively with other academics and colleagues, and remaining up to date with developments in the field including evidence-based assessment and therapeutic practices.
* Outstanding and sustained learning and teaching experience with demonstrated experience of involvement in course/curriculum development.
* Ability to proactively engage or partner with industry and professional bodies on relevant projects and to represent the School to external stakeholders and the general public.
* Demonstrated experience to make a contribution to the academic life and administrative tasks of the School and Faculty along with a track record of effective teamwork.

* Involve parents/carers in the educational process through ongoing, constructive dialogue.

* Produce diagnostic, formative, and summative assessments, utilising rubrics and visual evidence to track growth.

* Ensure positive transition experiences for boys moving across cohorts and stages.

* Coordinate, curate and mount student artwork for school displays, Speech Nights and the biennial Preparatory School Visual Arts Exhibition.

* Classroom Management: Proven ability to structure a productive, safe and positive studio routine while addressing various behaviours within a classroom context.
* Communication & Collaboration: Clear, empathetic and professional interpersonal communication skills with boys, colleagues and parents/carers.
* Digital Literacy: Practical competence in integrating ICT and educational software safely and creatively into classroom curricula.

* Knowledge of contemporary pedagogy tailored to boys’ education and development.
* In-depth understanding of child protection legislation, mandatory reporting protocols and studio risk management (materials, kilns, sharp instruments).
* Understanding of diverse cultural traditions, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives.

**Your role**

  

Drawing on your supervision experience, you will provide professional support, guidance and mentoring to the psychologist working within a multidisciplinary team of Human Resources, Judicial and Court Services staff.

  

The team provides direct psychological assessment, intervention, therapeutic services and educational support to District Court, Drug Court, Local Court, Children’s Court, Coroner’s Court Judges.

  

You will provide expert consultation to Judges regarding mental health and wellbeing, as well as providing advice and reporting to the Executive Team in line with the Psychological Support and Wellbeing Program.

  

**What you’ll do**

  

* Provide an ethical and effective psychology service in a dynamic environment for Judges who are charged with making significant legal decisions.
* Oversee all professional supervision, training, and development for psychologist/s in the team, including developing specific training for psychologist/s and other staff as required.
* Represent the Department externally in matters relating to psychology and related services.
* Maintain succinct documentation and psychological notes on all interactions with Judges receiving psychological services.
* Work in collaboration with the Judicial Commission and DCJ Executive, Present at conferences and events promoting the psychological services available to Judges.
  

**What we’re looking for**

  

* Experience in the development, establishment, and implementation of psychological services on a regional and/or state-wide basis.
* Experience in courts or legal settings is highly regarded, but not essential. Relevant experience may come from settings such as health, emergency services, defence, corrections, regulation or other complex public services.
* Expert knowledge and understanding of the complexities relating to the provision of psychological services within a complex environment.
* Thorough knowledge and understanding of the psychologist's ethical and legal obligations and professional accountability particularly the Court Services / CTSD / Judiciary policies and procedures.
* Experience in the professional supervision of psychologists.
  

**Essential Requirements**

  

* Post-graduate tertiary psychology qualifications at master’s level or higher, current full registration with the Psychology Board of Australia, and is eligible to be a Board-approved supervisor.
* Current driver’s licence with ability and willingness to travel throughout NSW.
